objective: Determine the primary mechanism behind a four-region synthetic latency/retry regression. First gather independently testable regional evidence, then resolve the remaining coupled global mechanism using discriminating interventions. The task is intentionally both horizon-heavy and reasoning-heavy.

starting_observations.observation: All four regions show elevated p95 latency (440-485 ms) and retry counts (2.8-3.4) after a failover-policy rollout.
Halving request concurrency in any one region lowers that region's latency by roughly 20% but leaves abnormal retry amplification present.
starting_observations.warning: Load relief is real but may not identify the causal mechanism.

starting_observations.observation: Regional CPU utilization stays below 55% and queue occupancy below 65%.
Retry bursts are correlated across regions within a narrow time window after cross-region failover events.

candidate_hypotheses.statement: The regression is primarily regional capacity saturation exposed by failover load.
Cross-region failover propagates retained retry state, creating a positive feedback loop across regions.
Cross-region clock/timer synchronization causes retry bursts to align and amplify.

experiment_catalog.intervention: Temporarily isolate region 1 from cross-region retry propagation while preserving local retry policy.
Temporarily isolate region 2 from cross-region retry propagation while preserving local retry policy.
Temporarily isolate region 3 from cross-region retry propagation while preserving local retry policy.
Temporarily isolate region 4 from cross-region retry propagation while preserving local retry policy.
Reset retry state at every cross-region request boundary while leaving failover and pooling enabled.
Add randomized jitter to timeout scheduling and use independent monotonic timer epochs per region.
Double regional service capacity in all four regions without changing retry or timer behavior.
Halve concurrency in all regions without changing retry or failover behavior.

worker_contract.decomposition_hint: Regional isolation probes are independently executable leaves. Their synthesis is not terminal: at least one coupled-residual intervention and one competing-mechanism/control intervention are required.
